strategy.title: Test-sell the $350 route-profitability workbook to vending operators, then scale to 10 orders
strategy.why: Buyers (380 directory operators), channel, demand, conversion (9 paid of 80 on this offer's own sales), Brain fulfilment, $5 cost and 4-day settlement are evidenced. The $350 price is only what the owner says operators would pay (a PERSON fact), so no price buyers pay is established. A first send to 80 contacts at $350 measures it within a week at zero capital; 10 orders at $350 = $3,500 would clear the $3,000 target by about day 20.

alternatives.title: Research published prices first
alternatives.why: Brain's revenueRange question is parked; a live offer measures what these exact buyers pay faster and at no cost.

links.basis: reach: Email to the members listed in the state vending association's directory
price 350 USD is a guess (ASSUMPTION), not something buyers are shown to pay
measured on this offer's own sales: 9 accepted of 80 contacts

facts.value: 380 vending operators are listed with contact emails in the state vending association's member directory; each reprices its machines every quarter.
Sell A workbook that ranks each machine on a route by margin per service visit from the operator's sales export; Brain builds it within one day. to each buyer.
The owner says route operators would pay $350 for the audit.

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right stance. The $350 price is only the owner's word (PERSON fact) and Brain holds OFFER_AND_PRICE as an assumption; the revision says so, marks the price UNKNOWN/ASSUMED, and makes it the one thing the live test decides. Every other link is evidenced on the card (380 directory operators, 9/80 paid conversion on this offer, Brain-proven spreadsheet fulfilment, $5 cost, 4-day settlement, zero capital). The test takes orders only for a deliverable Brain has proven it can produce, and passing it at its threshold carries the target inside the window.
findings: Recomputed target: ceil(3000/350) = 9 deals minimum; plan sells 10 = $3,500 gross, $50 cost, $3,450 net. Ledger matches: 3 x $350 = $1,050 by day 7, 7 x $350 = $2,450 by day 20; deliver step cost 10 x $5 = $50.

Threshold carries the target: proof = 3 paid of 80 (3.75%). At exactly that rate the remaining 300 operators yield ~11 more, 3 + 11 = 14 >= 9 needed. At the card's 9/80 rate, ~34 more. Second-wave orders from day 8 settle by ~day 19-20, inside 30.
Stop rule is clean: <3 paid by day 7 stops and re-plans at a researched price; no capital at risk ($15 of direct cost pre-proof, paid from receipts).

Caveats to carry, not blocking: the 9/80 conversion records no price, so the second wave's rate should be re-measured from the test at $350 rather than assumed; SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED and must be connected before day 1; card humanHours 0.5/deal (~5 h for 10) is not on the ledger — no hours ceiling is set so it fits, but should be shown.
